requirements.requirement_text:
The completed system must allow users to:

1. Open a dedicated Advanced Compositing Workspace.
2. Create compositions containing images, video, CGI, and VFX.
3. Organize content using editable layers and groups.
4. Create and connect compositing nodes.
5. Use layers and nodes through one shared compositing engine.
6. Combine images using correct alpha and blend operations.
7. Work with HDR and appropriate color management.
8. Import and use CGI render passes.
9. Composite CGI shadows and reflections onto footage.
10. Use depth for real/CGI occlusion.
11. Combine rotoscoping and keyed footage.
12. Use editable masks and matte processing.
13. Adjust exposure, white balance, curves, contrast, and colors.
14. Apply selective color correction.
15. Use color scopes.
16. Apply glow, blur, distortion, motion blur, and depth of field.
17. Composite particle effects, smoke, fire, and other VFX.
18. Use graph-generated VFX without losing event timing.
19. Create nested compositions and reusable node groups.
20. Expose parameters for easy adjustment.
21. Animate layers, node settings, and compositing effects through Kiwi's timeline.
22. Preserve source footage, tracking, CGI, and masks non-destructively.
23. Preview intermediate nodes and render passes.
24. Cache unchanged graph outputs efficiently.
25. Save complete editable compositions.
26. Reuse compositions and presets through project resources and Super Clipboard.
27. Export finished videos with synchronized audio.
28. Export transparent image sequences and supported HDR outputs.
29. Preserve correct timeline evaluation and source-frame timing.
30. Maintain good performance with scalable quality and cache settings.

**Do not implement the compositor as only a stack of full-screen filters.**

**Do not build a node editor that merely displays connected boxes without processing their data.**

**Do not implement separate incompatible layer and node compositing engines.**

**Do not flatten all render passes before the user can manipulate them.**

**Do not apply incorrect alpha mathematics that causes halos or transparency errors.**

**Do not confuse straight alpha with premultiplied alpha.**

**Do not blend scene-linear HDR values as though they were ordinary display-encoded colors.**

**Do not tone-map CGI more than once.**

**Do not force every intermediate result to 8-bit precision.**

**Do not compare incompatible depth representations.**

**Do not assume every CGI render pass is available through Godot's internal buffers without verification.**

**Do not make all CGI appear in front of real-world objects regardless of depth.**

**Do not implement color correction as only brightness and saturation sliders.**

**Do not implement masks as permanently destructive source-image changes.**

**Do not implement motion blur as only a generic blur with no motion information.**

**Do not regenerate upstream tracking, physics, or CGI geometry for appearance-only changes.**

**Do not depend on the number of output frames to determine physical simulation.**

**Do not require full-resolution rendering for every interactive preview operation.**

**Do not claim standard H.264 output supports transparent alpha.**

**Do not rebuild Kiwi's existing Image Workspace, Footage Manipulation, Motion Tracking, CGI Integration, VFX Graph, physics engine, or animation timeline.**

requirements.requirement_text:
**Kiwi Studios 2 should have a complete Advanced Compositing Workspace capable of combining real footage, animation, CGI, VFX, images, and render passes into professional-quality final scenes.**

A user should be able to import real footage, track the camera, reconstruct the environment, place a virtual 3D object, and open the result in the Compositing Workspace.

They should be able to independently control the CGI beauty, shadows, reflections, emission, and depth.

They should be able to use masks to place real people and objects in front of virtual geometry.

They should be able to match the CGI's exposure, colors, depth of field, motion blur, and grain to the original footage.

They should be able to add explosions, smoke, sparks, energy, and other procedural VFX while preserving the ability to edit individual layers and passes.

They should be able to work quickly using an intuitive layer stack, then build more complicated effects using a node graph.

The node graph should allow individual render passes and masks to be routed through color correction, blending, depth, and image-processing operations without destroying the original source content.

All compositions must remain non-destructive.

All parameters should remain editable and animatable.

All reusable effects should preserve their source relationships.

The compositor should evaluate the correct footage, tracking, animation, physics, and VFX state at every requested timeline time.

The final output should support high-quality rendering, appropriate HDR and alpha handling, and reliable video export.

**Make advanced compositing powerful enough for cinematic CGI and VFX production, flexible enough for stylized animation and 2D work, intuitive enough for ordinary editing, and deeply integrated with Kiwi Studios 2's existing modeling, animation, footage, physics, VFX, materials, and rendering systems.**
